about.title: Poway Slip & Fall & Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Poway's mix of shopping centers along Poway Road, retail plazas off Pomerado Road, and neighborhood businesses near Twin Peaks Road means residents and visitors are frequently walking through parking lots, entryways, and store aisles where hazards can go unaddressed. Wet floors, broken pavement, poor lighting, or unmarked steps can turn an ordinary errand into a serious injury. Under California law, a property owner or manager can be held responsible when they knew, or reasonably should have known, about a dangerous condition and failed to fix it or warn visitors. Proving that notice requires solid evidence — photos of the hazard, incident reports, and surveillance footage before it's deleted. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we're a free service that connects injured Poway residents with an independent attorney who can evaluate the property owner's knowledge, gather evidence, and pursue a claim on a contingency basis, meaning there's no fee unless you recover.

items.title: Notice Is Everything
items.desc: California premises liability claims hinge on proving the owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney can help identify how long a dangerous condition existed before your fall.

items.title: Time Limits Apply
items.desc: You generally have two years to file a claim, but that window shrinks significantly if a government entity owns the property. Acting quickly protects your options.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Shut You Out
items.desc: Even if you're partly at fault for not noticing a hazard, California's comparative fault rules mean you may still recover a reduced amount rather than nothing at all.

items.question: I fell at a store on Poway Road but didn't report it. Is it too late?
items.answer: Not necessarily, but the sooner you act the better, since surveillance video is often overwritten within days or weeks. An attorney can send a preservation request quickly to try to secure that footage before it's lost. You should also document the scene and your injuries as soon as possible.

items.question: What if the property owner says the hazard was obvious and I should have seen it?
items.answer: California follows a comparative fault system, so even if you're found partly responsible, you may still recover compensation reduced by your share of fault. This is a common defense tactic, and an attorney can help push back on it with evidence. Photos, witness statements, and lighting conditions all matter here.

items.question: Does it matter if my fall happened on public property in Poway?
items.answer: Yes — claims against government entities, like a city-owned sidewalk or public building, involve much shorter deadlines than the standard two years, sometimes just six months to file a claim. If your fall happened somewhere near a city facility or public walkway, it's important to get an attorney involved quickly to protect your rights.
